title: this is so much bigger than theatre. #hadestown #hadestowntour #hades...
transcript: This is one of the most devastating things I read in a very long time. Plato posted it yesterday and it's about J. Antonio Rodriguez, who was Orpheus on the Hades Town tour. Currently he is not allowed to perform because J Antonio immigrated with his family when he was just 2 years old. He remembers living nowhere else. Part of the reason they came to America is because he had childhood health issues that could only be resolved at hospitals in this country. But his family is undocumented cause of how young he was. J Antonio is a dreamer. Which is part of the Dhaka program, which is the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program, which was instituted by Obama in 2012. As soon as it was instituted, Antonio signed up. He's been part of that program since 2012 and it has allowed him, along with around 600,000 other people to live and work and go to school in this country without fear of being deported because it is the only place they have ever known. Dhaka is one of, if not the most important piece of immigration reform that has ever happened in this country. It is not a perfect program, not by any means, but it is critically important to the people that qualify for it. And it has been under constant attack since 2016 since probably for then as well. One of the things about Dhaka is you have to re renew every two years. Previously It would take two or three days for that to go through, but now there is a huge backlog in this country, and that is what is happening to J. Antonio. He has been waiting three months for his renewal to come through, and he is currently still with the tour. He is not allowed to be on stage. He is just there supporting his tour family and waiting. He has talked to lawyers, he has talked to the White House, and everyone just tells him it is a waiting game, which is unacceptable and there is not much we can do. But there is one small thing, extremely small thing, that we can, and we all need to do it right now. Group of Dreamers put together a change up, or petition asking the US Citizenship and Immigration Services Department to expedite Dhaka applications that are over 100 days old. It's literally like, the bare, bare minimum we can all do to go and sign this petition. They're asking for 7,005 messengers. They are very close, but I feel like we can blow this number out of the water. So sign it, share it. You have to. We all have to, because this is, like, the smallest thing you possibly do. This part of the article literally made me sob when I read it, because it's about how Orpheus's story is very much a story of immigration and him not having the right documentation. And literally a song called papers like Just the idea of the fact that, like, Jan, Tony has been dealing with this and having to sing the song every single night and having to sing if it's true every single night. And I just. I don't know. I wish there was something we can do. And the only thing I can think of right now is to just try and raise awareness any way we can. For all of us to go and sign that change out or petition and to just share it with everybody that we know. I heart breaks for J. Antonio. This is a horribly broken system that he has found himself in. Learn and educate ourselves, especially now that we are in an election cycle to try and push for better immigration reform, a more compassionate immigration reform, a more equitable immigration reform. Go sign the petition. Go read about Dhaka and other Dhaka recipients. Go learn more about what we can do. I also need to do that because I just wanna cry. We're here for you, Jay. Anything we can do, please let me know.
classificationReason: Discusses immigration issues affecting Hadestown tour cast member, not reviewing the production itself
